mechanism: Isocarboxazid (MAOI) inhibits monoamine oxidase while darunavir is a CYP3A4 substrate that can elevate sympathomimetic amines; combined use risks hypertensive crisis, serotonin syndrome, and increased darunavir levels via potential metabolic interactions.
action: Avoid concurrent use; if both agents are necessary, select an alternative antiretroviral (non-CYP3A4 dependent) and monitor blood pressure and mental status closely.
